header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Redwood: Jordan Reed (AE), Samir Patel (SE)
Aurelia Health: Marta Lopez (Head of ML), Derek Chen (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Security), Oliver Park (Data Scientist)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review results from last week's model comparisons, discuss version pinning and fallback/rollback strategy. Primary focus: pick a candidate model for pilot, confirm perf tradeoffs (latency vs cost), and align on next steps for stability testing and security review. Customer is leaning toward private deployment eventually but will pilot on hosted first to speed iteration. Open questions remain around exact pinning granularity (major vs patch), acceptable rollback windows, and SLOs for canary/rollouts.
topics: version pinning strategy and rollback/fallback policies
latency and throughput numbers from last benchmark
quantization tradeoffs and impact on accuracy
security/PII concerns: KMS, data residency, SOC2/HIPAA
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Reed: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh it's our weekly poc sync for aurelia, good to see you all.
00:12 Marta Lopez: hey jordan thanks, quick call today, we have a couple results to go over and then we need to lock model pinning.
00:22 Samir Patel: yes i'll start with the perf summary from the bench we ran tuesday. so we compared rdx-3b-open and rdx-7b-quant and also a public 7b variant from upstream, um the numbers: hosted baseline (rdx-3b) avg token lat 70ms, 95p 210ms; rdx-7b-quant avg token 120ms, 95p 420ms but cost per request ~0.38x higher vs 3b.
00:45 Derek Chen: those 95p numbers for the 7b look a bit high given our seq length, what's the seqlen distribution in that benchmark?
00:55 Samir Patel: good call. the test used seq up to 1024 for worst-case; typical user median is 150 tokens so p95 also drops ~25% in that traffic mix. the 420ms is worst-case when KV cache miss and long prefix.
01:12 Marta Lopez: accuracy tradeoffs? we saw recall drop on medical entity extraction for quantized 7b.
01:20 Samir Patel: yes quant-7b had a measured recall 90.8% vs rdx-3b at 88.9% for the specific clinical NER eval set — so quant can actually help or hurt depending on the task, weird but consistent. cliff notes: 7b gives quality lift on generation tasks but for NER maybe model architecture matters more.
01:38 Oliver Park: hmm interesting. so for our use-case (clinical summarization + redaction) where precision on entities is important, maybe 7b is worth the latency/cost bump.
01:48 Priya Singh: security question — if we pin to a hosted model variant, what are our guarantees on model updates? we can't have silent changes to weights.
02:00 Jordan Reed: absolutely — that's why pinning exists. redwood supports pin-by-version (we can pin the exact model hash) and also policy-based rollbacks. the default hosted flow is we pin to a specific model version and any model updates require an opt-in.
02:15 Priya Singh: ok and audit logs? we need proof of what model served which request for compliance.
02:22 Samir Patel: audit logs are included, token-level traces with model id and version, plus we can integrate to your SIEM. for private deployments you'll also get private KMS integration.
02:33 Derek Chen: let's talk rollback/fallback strategy — we want automatic fallbacks to a cheaper model if latency SLO breaks. is that supported?
02:42 Jordan Reed: yes, you can define routing policies: latency-first will route to faster variants, or you can say mandatory pinned and manual rollback only. typical pattern: canary 10% on new variant, monitor metrics for 24-72h, automatic rollback if error/latency thresholds exceeded.
02:58 Marta Lopez: what about pinning granularity? major vs minor patch? we had issues with minor patches changing logits.
03:07 Samir Patel: recommended: pin entire model hash for production pilot; during experimental phase pin by minor release to allow non-breaking infra fixes. we can also provide a deployment config that pins kernel/quantization profile separately.
03:25 Jordan Reed: reminder — for the pilot we suggested rdx-7b-quant v1.2 (the one in the spreadsheet) as candidate A and rdx-3b-stable as fallback.
03:36 Oliver Park: can we get a quick A/B on generation quality vs NER recall? maybe split 50/50 for 48h?
03:44 Samir Patel: yes we can set up route 50/50 and collect eval metrics. for budget reasons maybe 24h is enough to see signal, but 48h better.
03:55 Priya Singh: on data residency — we will need logs kept in our region and ensure PII redaction before export. is that possible with hosted?
04:04 Jordan Reed: hosted can be region pinned, but if you need full control we recommend private deployment (VPC). for the POC many customers do hosted region-pinned and then upgrade to private for compliance.
04:15 Marta Lopez: ok timeline — we want to pick a pinned model by next sync and run a 24h stability load.
04:22 Derek Chen: if we run the stability test, can we use your continuous batching and KV cache config recommendations?
04:30 Samir Patel: yes will share config — batch sizes, warmup scripts, and cache priming steps. note: cache priming reduces first-token latency significantly.
04:39 Jordan Reed: quick note on cost — 7b quant with autoscale steady-state approx 1.9x cost vs 3b but unit quality higher for summarization.
04:48 Marta Lopez: are there any competitor pros/cons we should call out?
04:52 Jordan Reed: we briefly compared with OpenAI and Anthropic; main differences are transparency on model versions and deployment flexibility — redwood gives you version pinning and private options; OpenAI is simple but less control, Anthropic we saw similar quality but cost/latency tradeoffs.
05:06 Oliver Park: small nit: transcription in your spreadsheet had some mismatched model names (rdx vs rdxn), please fix so we can map configs.
05:14 Jordan Reed: noted, will clean up and reupload.
05:17 Marta Lopez: ok let's run through concrete next actions — who does what.
05:22 Jordan Reed: samir will run the 24h stability on the candidate we pin (rdx-7b-quant v1.2) and produce a perf + error report, i'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and security checklist, marta please confirm acceptance criteria and priya to review the KMS/PII notes.
05:40 Priya Singh: one security detail — we require rotated keys every 90 days and HSM-backed root keys if we go private, i'll send a short note after this call.
05:48 Samir Patel: got it. i'll include key rotation considerations in the deployment notes.
05:52 Derek Chen: last question on rollback timing — can we set a cool-down window so automatic rollback doesn't flip flappy under short spikes?
06:01 Samir Patel: yes you can set sustained-window thresholds, e.g., 5 minute median and 30 minute sustained to avoid noise.
06:10 Jordan Reed: great, i'll capture all that in the next email. anything else?
06:14 Marta Lopez: not from me, good sync.
06:15 Jordan Reed: thanks all, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and tests.
06:20 [call ends]

Notes on transcription: minor mislabels and occasional filler words remain; speaker turns approximate.
